steps.say: This is a sixteen-line LiDAR on a motor, its sweeps stacked as they arrive. A ball of streaks.
Turn the sensor while it spins and every return is measured from a different angle.

scenes.headline: alpha-LiDAR: a LiDAR on a motor
scenes.sub: Why turn the sensor, and the filter that keeps up
scenes.say: I'm Swivel. Here is why alpha-LiDAR turns an ordinary LiDAR, and what its code does to keep up.

labels: Upright: a band, blind above and below
On its side, motor still: one slice
Motor turning: the slice sweeps the sphere
Focus sweep: returns pile up ahead

steps.say: Unroll the sphere around the sensor. Upright, sixteen lines cover a band about thirty degrees tall.
steps.term: Band: the only directions an upright LiDAR sees

steps.say: Lay it on its side and each revolution becomes a vertical fan.
Now let the motor turn it. Within a second the fan has passed through every direction.
Swing it back and forth instead, and the returns concentrate where you point it.

steps.caption: Hesai, RoboSense and Livox heads
steps.say: The head takes several LiDARs. A gimbal motor with a built-in encoder turns it.

steps.caption: IMU on the head, encoder on the motor
steps.say: The IMU rides on the head with the LiDAR, so it feels the motor's turn directly.

stations.label: Deskew
stations.sub: each return to the sweep's end

steps.say: Integrate the IMU through the sweep and move every return to the pose at the sweep's end. That is FAST-LIO2's deskew.
Each return carries a covariance, and an angle error grows with range.
Far, uncertain returns count less when they are matched to the plane map.
The motor encoder never enters the filter. It only re-expresses the pose for whatever carries the head.

left.title: Non-static start
items: attitude from the IMU's own orientation
gravity straight down, bias at zero
left.say: Its first change: start while the head is already spinning, using the orientation the IMU reports.

right.title: Uncoupled encoder
right.say: Its second: the motor angle, used only to give the pose of the base.

steps.caption: 17.3 ms mean latency
steps.say: The repo's own run: about seventeen milliseconds a scan.

steps.caption: segmented ATE 0.05988 m
steps.say: And six centimetres of error, averaged over windows of two hundred poses, each aligned on its own. A kind metric.

scenes.title: Spinning head, error over 24.3 m
scenes.note: Synthetic, exact truth; FAST-LIO2 diverged at every rate
scenes.say: On a synthetic head already spinning when the recording starts, alpha-LiDAR holds a few centimetres up to six radians a second. FAST-LIO2, starting the usual static way, drifts off by kilometres.

scenes.title: Motor removed: Oxford walk, 283 m
scenes.note: Same machine, same harness, fixed sensor
scenes.say: Take the motor away and it is still a good odometry: four point four six centimetres on an Oxford walk, ahead of FAST-LIO2 and PV-LIO on the same machine.

scenes.text: Turn the sensor, keep the IMU on the head, and the same filter keeps up.
scenes.mark: keep the IMU on the head
